history.p: Gade started working on "Psyche" in the spring of 1877. However, after having finished the first part, he got ill and had to put it aside. Furthermore, the Senate of the University of Copenhagen asked him in March 1878 to write a cantata for the celebration of the 400th anniversary of the University. It was not until the summer of 1880 that he asked the Birmingham Festival whether they would be interested in a new major oratorio from his hand. They accepted his offer, and "Psyche" had its first performance on 31 August 1882.

Ah me! far from the home I long for

Psyche, hear thou what we have to teach thee
Wo bin ich? Dunkel mich umhüllt
Where am I? Darkness wraps me round
There comes with waving dusky robes bedight

Eros! Ich fühl's, ich fühl's, dein Herz mir jetzt Verzeihung gab
Eros, I feel thy heart at last can pardon shew
Breit' aus die Flügel ohne Furcht und Beben
Spread out thy pinions, on their strength relying

physDesc.physMedium: 17 bifolios and 9 single folios. Written in ink and pencil. One bifolio used as cover; with inscription in pencil: "1ste Udkast / til Compositionen / Psyche". On fol.1.r in lower right-hand corner Gade has written: "Begyndt 1 Juni 18877."; "1877" repeated in pencil. Many different paginations. With numerous emendations and cancellations. On a bifolio containing sketches for no. 10 dated "3 August / 1877." Sketch for "III Im Hades" dated "20 September / 77". With Danish text.
Written in ink. Paper: 9, 14, 18, 20 staves. Sporadic pagination: 23-26, 23-25, 49-56 and 71-85. Last page blank. With German text.
1 single folio. Written in ink. Paper: 20 staves. With numerous cancellations.

Written in ink. Paper: 18 staves (pp. 1-48); 20 staves ( pp. 49-85). Paginated 1-85; last page blank. With emendations and cancellations. At the end of Part One on p. 25 dated: "Vedbæk. / 27 Aug 1881." At the end of Part Four on p. 85 Gade has written: "S.D.G. / Fine. / [Gade's musical signature] / 14 Decbr. 1881.". With German text.
